clue.text: Ribbon — something stunning on a dog

parts.note: a bow is a ribbon tied in loops
a wow is a sensational success, something that stuns onlookers

explanation.surface: A dog is decked out with a ribbon that makes it look stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a nursery word: small children call a dog by its bark.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's imitative word for a dog, taken from the sound of its barking.

clue.text: Opposes dangerous sort of ammunition

parts.note: to buck a trend or a system is to oppose or resist it
hot can mean dangerous, as in a situation too hot to handle

explanation.surface: Someone resists a particularly hazardous kind of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead pellets fired in quantity from a shotgun are a type of ammunition.

clue.text: River runs into Welsh property owners' dockside locations

indicators.note: the river runs into the other pieces, so its letter is set inside them

parts.note: the haves are those who own property, as opposed to the have-nots

explanation.surface: A river flows into Welsh landowners' quayside sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs into' puts R inside W + HAVES, after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Landing stages where ships tie up are places along the dockside.

clue.text: Runner ignores a tricky run

indicators.note: something tricky is twisted and awkward, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An athlete skips an awkward lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete, but it is the definition: someone who runs an event. 'tricky' is the anagram signal for 'ignores a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs or arranges an event or business is the person in charge of organising it.

clue.text: Island's main road going between two preserves

indicators.note: the road goes between the two preserves, so its letters sit between them

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
to can food is to preserve it, and a can is a tin of preserved food
A1 is Britain's main road north, written here as AI

explanation.surface: An island's principal highway runs between two jam factories.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, from London to Edinburgh; the digit 1 serves as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for things belonging to the Caribbean island whose capital is Kingston.

clue.text: In disarray, like retail managers, collectively?

explanation.surface: A chaotic store where the managers are spread through every department.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition takes the idiom literally: between them, managers of a shop are present everywhere in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for scattered and disorganised; literally, spread throughout a store.

clue.text: Shock announcement made by a missionary

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so it is the sound of the words that counts

parts.note: Paul, the apostle, was the great missionary of the early church, so this is 'a Paul'

explanation.surface: A preacher says something shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Paul' said aloud sounds like the verb meaning to horrify.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay or horrify someone is to give them a nasty jolt.

clue.text: Set of cutlery, and where it could be used

explanation.surface: A box of knives and forks and the place where you would eat with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxed set of cutlery shares its name with a workplace dining room.

clue.text: Nodding head, worker follows on

indicators.note: the worker comes after the head, so its letters are placed second

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A head of department nods off while a worker carries on.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare botanical word for a flower that droops or nods on its stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical adjective for drooping flower heads that hang down as if bowing.

clue.text: Frankly, how does an eleven-man soccer squad play?

definitions.text: how does an eleven-man soccer squad play?

explanation.surface: A candid question about a football team with no substitutes.
explanation.walkthrough: A football side is eleven players, so an eleven-man squad has no substitute on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means candidly, holding nothing back; literally, with no substitutes available.

clue.text: Slight reduction in price coming on stream for barbecue

indicators.note: a slight reduction trims the word by its last letter

parts.note: a charge is the price asked for something
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A modest price cut appears on a grill by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight reduction in' takes the E off CHARGE, leaving CHARG.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook food over a hot grill so it is seared, as on a barbecue.

clue.text: Advice about storing new and old wine

indicators.note: the reversed advice holds the other letters inside it as a cellar stores bottles
about means turned round, so the word for advice is read backwards

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: A tip on laying down wines both young and old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TIP into PIT, and 'storing' puts N and O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grape variety and the wine made from it, such as Pinot Noir.

clue.text: Part of contest is held in silence

indicators.note: the contest is held inside the call for silence

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
an event is a contest in a sports meeting

explanation.surface: A round of a competition takes place without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: One of seven equal portions into which something is divided.

clue.text: Sick humour about peasant

indicators.note: the humour goes about the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: vein can mean mood or humour, as in in a comic vein
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A peasant's bad-tempered mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humour' is the old word for mood or temperament, as in in a good humour, which is why vein fits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval serf, a feudal tenant tied to the land, is a kind of peasant.

clue.text: Ocean, for instance, is a source of water

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ocean
as can mean for instance, as in big cats such as lions
taken as written

explanation.surface: The ocean is held up as an example of where water comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert where there is water from a spring or well.

clue.text: Raising Union Jack about start of procession

indicators.note: the Union and Jack pieces together go about the starting letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, and a rating is a sailor in the ranks

indicators.note: the first letter of procession is taken

explanation.surface: A Union Jack is hoisted as a parade begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union Jack' looks like the flag, but splits into U and RATING; 'about' sets P between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Increasing a rate or value, such as uprating a pension, means raising it.

clue.text: A new Satie composition, oriental in character

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly written piece by Erik Satie with an Eastern flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges A NEW SATIE. Satie was a French composer, which makes 'composition' look like music.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the island nation off the Chinese mainland, an East Asian people.

clue.text: Give over walkin' up and down without clothes

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the walking word goes round the clothes

parts.note: pacin', with the g dropped, is walking up and down
kit is a set of clothes, as in sports kit

explanation.surface: Stop strolling to and fro with nothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The dropped g in 'walkin'' tells you the walking word drops its g too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British phrases meaning stop it or quit doing that.

clue.text: Scholar has restored painting brought in for each church

indicators.note: the restored painting is brought inside the word for each

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head

indicators.note: restoring repairs and rebuilds, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: art is painting and the like

explanation.surface: A scholar has a restored painting brought into every church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scholar' points to the Italian poet, revered by Renaissance humanists as the first great classical scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourteenth-century Italian poet was also a leading humanist scholar.

clue.text: First bit of yoghurt stirred in muesli mixture — heaven!

indicators.note: the yoghurt's letter is stirred into the cereal, set inside it
a mixture is jumbled, so the letters of muesli are rearranged
the first letter of yoghurt is taken

explanation.surface: A spoonful of yoghurt mixed into muesli is bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges MUESLI into ELSIUM, and 'stirred in' places Y after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Elysian Fields were the paradise of the blessed dead.

clue.text: God essentially behind rains

indicators.note: the answer is in the essence or heart of these words, buried in them

explanation.surface: A deity is fundamentally the force behind the rains.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'behind' and the start of 'rains'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu deity of thunder, rain and war, king of the gods in the Vedas.

clue.text: Is Venus so shapely?

parts.note: Venus is the goddess of beauty, so the clue asks whether she has the form of a god, not just a lovely figure

explanation.surface: A question about the goddess of love's good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means having the form of a god, which a goddess must literally have.

clue.text: With difficulty move articles in storage

explanation.surface: Lugging heavy furniture into a storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the second sense is old disused furniture, kept in a lumber room.
explanation.definitionFit: To move clumsily and heavily; also a British word for stored junk.

clue.text: Grant the president may be a hero?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a US president counts as a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses S. Grant was US president; the same name is the Latin form of Odysseus, the Greek hero.
explanation.definitionFit: First name of President Grant, and the Latin name of the wandering Greek hero of Homer.

clue.text: Portion of asparagus served for starters with avocado?

indicators.note: for starters means taking the first letter of served

parts.note: the avocado is also called the avocado pear

explanation.surface: Asparagus served as a starter with avocado.
explanation.definitionFit: A single shoot or stalk of asparagus is called a spear.

clue.text: Plant, a variety of spikenard? No way

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RD, road, is a way, and no way means those letters are lost from the mix

explanation.surface: Asking whether a plant is a type of spikenard and being told certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIKENARD has the letters of the answer plus RD (road, a way), which 'No way' takes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift, a coastal plant with pink flowers, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Trees said to provide cover

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for trees is heard rather than seen

parts.note: bays are bay trees, laurels

explanation.surface: Trees are said to give shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the green cloth covering a snooker or card table.
explanation.definitionFit: Green woollen cloth used to cover card tables and snooker tables.

clue.text: Removed from base, being audibly advised to take roads abroad

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a traveller routed out is sent out on a route abroad

explanation.surface: Someone is uprooted, being told aloud which roads to take overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'routed out' and the answer sound the same in British speech, where route rhymes with root.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulled up by the roots, so taken out from its base or origin.

clue.text: Observer one employed in exam grade dispute?

definitions.text: one employed in exam grade dispute?

explanation.surface: An onlooker hired when there is a row over exam results.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as re-marker: someone who marks a contested paper again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who passes a comment; also, read as re-marker, an examiner who marks again.

clue.text: Don't worry, Ned's gone outside to find the pests

indicators.note: the letters of Ned have gone from the outer parts of the phrase

parts.note: never mind means don't worry
the name Ned, spelt as written

explanation.surface: Telling someone not to fret because Ned has gone out to deal with the pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone outside' removes N and E from the front and D from the end of NEVERMIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats, mice and other troublesome creatures are collectively vermin.
